title: Console adoption rollup tables and upstream data contracts
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create a new set of curated adoption and engagement rollup tables for the Console product that serve BI, growth, and SRE use cases. Define stable upstream data contracts and transformation rules so downstream dashboards and alerts have predictable semantics. Deliver daily and hourly grains, SCD handling for workspace and user attributes, and a clear backfill and rollout plan.
background: Current console usage dashboards query a mix of event-level tables with ad-hoc joins. This causes inconsistent metric definitions (e.g., active workspace vs workspace seen), repeated heavy queries, and fragile dashboards when upstream event schemas change. We need a canonical layer that codifies adoption metrics (e.g., workspace-first-generation, feature adoption by route/model, latency cohorts) with traceability back to raw events.
goals: 1) Provide a set of curated 'console_adoption_*' tables (daily / hourly) consumed by Looker and internal analytic jobs. 2) Publish upstream data contracts documenting source fields, expected cardinality, null semantics, and retention. 3) Implement SCD2 for workspace metadata and TTL for high-cardinality route/model tags. 4) Ensure production-quality testing, backfill, and monitoring.
out_of_scope: Live query optimization for the realtime route (streams) index, embedding store refactor, and changes to client telemetry SDKs.
design_summary: We will introduce two fact tables: console_adoption_hourly (hourly grain, per workspace-route-model combination) and console_adoption_daily (daily rollup). Dimension tables: dim_workspace_scd (SCD2 for billing tier, org size), dim_route (low-cardinality route metadata), dim_model_variant (model family + quantization tag). Upstream contract docs will live in Confluence and be enforced via CI checks on event schema PRs. Partitioning: daily by date, hourly by date + hour; clustered on workspace_id and route_id. For attributes that change (workspace name, tier), use SCD2 with effective_from/effective_to. Backfill uses staged incremental jobs with checkpointing and validation queries.
schema_changes:
- Create console_adoption_hourly(date, hour, workspace_id, route_id, model_family, requests_count, tokens_in, tokens_out, p95_latency_ms, unique_users, first_time_flag, source_event_ids[]).
- Create console_adoption_daily(date, workspace_id, route_id, model_family, requests_count, tokens_in, tokens_out, p95_latency_ms, weekly_active_users_estimate).
- dim_workspace_scd(workspace_id, workspace_key, effective_from, effective_to, billing_tier, region, is_enterprise).
partition_strategy: console_adoption_hourly partitioned by date; sub-partition by hour using integer range. Tables clustered on (workspace_id, route_id) for query locality. dim_workspace_scd partitioned by effective_from month for efficient historical joins.
data_contracts_and_validation: Data contract doc URL included in attachments. Validation rules: non-null workspace_id on final rollups, tokens_in/tokens_out must be >= 0, p95_latency_ms computed from raw latency distribution, sampling tolerance <= 1% vs raw event aggregates. Implement a pre-commit SQL linter and CI unit tests for transformation macros.
backfill_strategy: 1) Snapshot current raw event timestamps for range 2023-01-01 -> now. 2) Run rolling backfills in 7-day windows with dedupe on source_event_ids. 3) Validate counts and p95 against baseline dashboards. 4) Throttle backfill clusters to avoid impact on production warehouse. 5) Mark backfill windows as complete in metadata table.
migration_steps:
- Add new tables in read-replica schema.
- Deploy transformation jobs (hourly first, then daily).
- Run backfill for historical data.
- Switch Looker dashboards to new tables behind a feature flag.
- Monitor discrepancies for 72 hours; if stable, flip default datasource and deprecate legacy queries.
acceptance_criteria:
- Looker 'Console Overview' and 'Adoption Funnels' show metrics within 2% of previous baseline after switching.
- SCD2 dimension includes historical rows and queries can join via effective date window.
- Backfill completes for last 18 months with discrepancy report passed.
- CI checks for data contract violations fail PRs with clear error messages.
- Monitoring: scheduled daily data quality job reports < 0.5% failed rows.
monitoring_and_alerting: Set up DataDog alerts on job failure, row count drift (>3% vs previous day), and latency increases in transform processing. Publish Looker health dashboard for weekly review. Add SLA badge to pipeline run if >95% of hourly runs complete within 30 minutes.
rollback_plan: If a discrepancy >5% is detected on key adoption metrics after toggling dashboards, revert Looker data source to legacy tables and pause the transform jobs. Investigate with playbook: compare raw event aggregates, re-run backfill for suspect windows, open a hotfix PR for transformation logic.
security_and_privacy_considerations: Avoid storing raw user identifiers in curated tables; use stable hashed identifiers (workspace_id, hashed_actor_id) and redact any PII. Access to dim_workspace_scd includes admin-only columns that require row-level security. KMS-encrypted metadata for backfill checkpoints.
tasks: Draft data contract Confluence page and link to event schema definitions
Implement SQL transforms for hourly rollup (dbt models + tests)
Create SCD2 dimension model and tests
Add CI checks for data contract violations on event schema PRs
Prepare backfill orchestration jobs with checkpointing
Run staged backfill for most recent 6 months and validate
Switch 3 priority Looker dashboards behind feature flag
Create monitoring dashboards and DataDog alerts
Post-mortem template & runbook for metric discrepancies
comments: 2025-02-14 Maya Patel: Initial scoping complete. Spoke with Growth to confirm priority metrics (workspace activation, daily active workspace by feature).
2025-02-20 Noah Grant: POC hourly model implemented in a scratch schema. Early p95 compute looks higher than old approach; investigating percentile algorithm differences.

2025-02-27 Jordan Kim (data eng review): Recommend storing sample_event_ids limited to 100 per row to enable traceability without exploding storage. Also suggested using approx_percentile for p95 to speed calculations in backfill.
2025-03-01 Sasha Rivera (growth PM): Approved schema and contract doc draft; asked for an additional column 'first_seen_via' to trace acquisition channel — added to backlog for next iteration.

2025-03-04 Ops: Ran a small backfill window (2025-02-01 -> 2025-02-07). Observed 0.9% row mismatch on unique_users vs raw events; acceptable under current tolerance. No performance impact on nightly ETL.

2025-03-05 Noah Grant: Created initial PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/analytics/pull/1287 with dbt models and tests. CI failing on one test (non-null tokens_in) due to an upstream event variant; raised ENG-52130 to track upstream fix.
notes: Design decision: prefer SCD2 for workspace metadata to support historical cohorting for billing and retention analysis.
Trade-off: storing a small array of source_event_ids increases storage but significantly reduces time-to-debug for metric deltas.
Future: consider a materialized aggregated metric service for sub-second dashboard interactivity; OOB for this ticket.
Related to ENG-43127 and ENG-34720 but focused specifically on adoption/feature usage metrics and stable contracts.
